nodes.characterization_summary: Surface of CoW/CF covered by microparticles with average size of ≈2.4 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface of CoW/CF is observed to be covered by microparticles with an average size of ≈2.4 μm as revealed by the field-emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM) image (Figure 1b; Figure S5, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings demonstrate uniform distribution of Co and W elements on the CF surface in CoW/CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mappings demonstrate a uniform distribution of Co and W elements on the CF surface in CoW/CF (Figure 1c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co/CF shows three low-intensity peaks of metallic Co (JCPDS:05-0727), indicating low crystallinity. CoW/CF shows vanished peaks confirming amorphous nature; after heat treatment at 873K, peaks arise with low-angle shift between metallic Co and W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern for Co/CF (Figure 1e) presents three low-intensity peaks corresponding to metallic (JCPDS:05-0727), indicating that Co/CF is in low crystallinity. After the addition of W, the three peaks completely vanished... after heat treatment at 873K for 3h in Ar, the three diffraction peaks for CoW/CF arise with a slight low-angle shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Co and W in CoW/CF. Co 2p peaks shift from 778.1/793.1 eV (Co⁰ in Co/CF) to 778.6/793.6 eV in CoW/CF indicating electron transfer from Co to W; W 4f peaks at 31.59/33.73 eV confirm metallic W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen that only the element of Co is presented in the XPS survey spectrum of Co/CF, while both Co and W elements exist in that of CoW/CF... The binding energies (BEs) of Co 2p in Co/CF... 778.1/793.1 eV... Co 2p in CoW/CF... 778.6/793.6 eV... BEs of W 4f in CoW/CF... 31.59/33.73 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoW/CF exhibits smaller charge transfer resistance than Co/CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) can measure the ability of charge transfer. As expected, CoW/CF exhibits a smaller charge transfer resistance (Figure S14, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance Cdl from CV at different scan rates gives ECSA of CoW/CF as 1625 cm² (larger than Co/CF 1490 cm²); annealed CoW/CF shows 265 cm² confirming low-crystallinity increases active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of the materials is determined via the double layer capacitance (Cdl) according to cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests with different scan rates... the ECSA of CoW/CF is tested to be 1625 cm²... larger than that of Co/CF (1490 cm²)... smaller ECSA of the annealed CoW/CF (265 cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 1150 cm⁻¹ (*NH₂) and 1483 cm⁻¹ (NH₄⁺) observed for CoW/CF and Co/CF from 0 to -0.8 V, stronger for CoW/CF indicating higher NH₃ yield.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis demonstrates that when using a catalyst of CoW/CF or Co/CF, two peaks at 1150 cm⁻¹ (*NH₂) and 1483 cm⁻¹ (NH₄⁺) are observed... However, the peaks obtained with CoW/CF catalyst are slightly stronger than those of Co/CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Molar ratio of Co:W confirmed as 0.87:0.13.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The exact molar ratio of Co:W is confirmed to be 0.87:0.13 through the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-AES, Table S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: After 20h stability test, morphology of CoW/CF remains similar to initial state and elemental ratio of Co to W is basically unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the recycling test, the morphology of CoW/CF (Figure S17, Supporting Information) remains similar to its initial state, and the SEM-EDS results show that the elemental ratio of Co to W is basically unchanged before and after the reaction (Table S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoW/CF maintains low-crystallinity/amorphous state after 20h recycling test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, CoW/CF maintains its low-crystallinity/amorphous state after recycling application (Figure S18, Supporting Information).
